 2026/27 SINGAPORE PREMIER LEAGUE MATCHWEEK 5: ROUNDUP
 26 October, 2026 
 SINGAPORE, 26 OCTOBER 2026 – Tampines Rovers maintained their perfect start to the 2026/27 Singapore Premier League (SPL) season with a victory over FC Jurong, while defending champions Lion City Sailors and Geylang International overcame Tanjong Pagar United and Hougang United respectively to extend their unbeaten runs. Elsewhere, Balestier Khalsa edged past Young Lions to round off a month without defeat. We recap all the action here…
 Spirited Young Lions fall to narrow defeat 
 Young Lions 1-2 Balestier | Jalan Besar | 24 October 
 Shuya Yamashita 45+4’ | Tin Matic 5’, Hiro Mizuguchi 22’ 
 Matic steered home Jakov Katusa’s cross to give Balestier an early lead in the fifth minute, before Mizuguchi doubled the Tigers’ advantage in the 22nd minute with a low drive into the bottom corner. Yamashita then pulled one back for the hosts on the stroke of half-time, rising highest to head home Hafiz Nor’s pinpoint free-kick.
 The hosts emerged from the break with renewed vigour but were unable to find an equaliser as Balestier held on to claim all three points.
 Facts 
 Balestier extended their winning run against the Young Lions to five games, with their last defeat coming on 25 January 2025. 
 Balestier ended October unbeaten with two wins and a draw, bouncing back from defeats in their opening two SPL matches in September.
 Hiro Mizuguchi scored his first goal for Balestier. 
 Shuya Yamashita scored his first goal for the Young Lions. 
 Daniel Goh made his 100th appearance for Balestier. 
 Young Lions’ Sarrvin Raj made his first SPL start.
 Young Lions: Izwan Mahbud (GK), Fairuz Fazli, Shuya Yamashita, Nathan Mao (C) (Ajay Robson 46’), Kai Whitmore, Hafiz Nor (Andy Reefqy 83’), Iryan Fandi, Joel Chew (Lukyan Tan 89’), Garv Sahoo (Ikram Mikhail 89’), Sarrvin Raj (Toi Kagami 46’), Hisatoshi Nishido
 Unused subs: Jeremy Quan (GK), Kenneth Ng (GK), Caelan Cheong, Nyqil Iyyan, Elijah Srinivasa, Abdil Qaiyyim, Jovan Ang
 Balestier: Mario Mustapic (GK), Azim Akbar (Syafi Nur Hilman 83’), Tajeli Salamat (C), Daniel Goh (Ikmal Hazlan 83’), Marin Kuzminski (Zikos Chua 90+6’), Woo Chun Wei (Ilyasin Zayan 90+6’), Hiro Mizuguchi, Tin Matic, Yushin Otake, Jakov Katusa, Fudhil I’yadh
 Unused subs: Hafiz Ahmad (GK), Dany Irfan (GK), Danial Crichton, Timothy Cheng, Ethan Pinto, Irfan Mika’il, Ramadhan Putera
 Sailors run riot against Jaguars 
 Sailors 6-0 Tanjong Pagar | Jalan Besar | 25 October 
 Hugo Gomes 37’, Matthias Phaeton 60’, Antonio Mance 70’, 90+3’, Giovanni Haag 87’, Hariss Harun 90+5’ 
 Lion City Sailors produced a ruthless second-half display to cruise to a commanding 6-0 victory over Tanjong Pagar United. 
 Gomes broke the deadlock in the 37th minute with a stunning long-range effort before the floodgates opened after the break. 
 Phaeton doubled their advantage on the hour mark with a precise finish into the bottom corner, before Mance glanced home Diogo Costa’s cross from the left in the 70th minute. 
 Haag added a fourth three minutes from time with a clever free-kick that sneaked under the Tanjong Pagar wall, before Mance grabbed his second of the evening with a first-time effort that Aitor Mujica could only spill into the net.
 Hariss completed the rout in the fifth minute of stoppage time, heading home at the far post.
 Facts 
 Hariss Harun scored his first SPL goal since 2 October 2022, when he found the net in the Sailors’ 5-3 defeat to Balestier. 
 Sailors have now won 21 consecutive matches against Tanjong Pagar and remain unbeaten in all 22 meetings with the Jaguars since the club’s inception in 2020.
 This is the ninth time the Sailors have scored six or more goals against Tanjong Pagar in an SPL fixture. 
 Sailors: Victor Aznar (GK), Jeorge Karseladze (Giovanni Haag 46’), Hugo Gomes, Lionel Tan (Hariss Harun 65’), Kyoga Nakamura, Bart Ramselaar (Antonio Mance 65’), Song Uiyoung (Farhan Zulkifli 46’), Ilhan Fandi (Shawal Anuar 65’), Matthias Phaeton, Bailey Wright (C), Diogo Costa
 Unused subs: Adib Azahari (GK), Ivan Susak (GK), Toni Datkovic, Glenn Kweh, Hami Syahin, Abdul Rasaq, Nur Muhammad Asis
 Tanjong Pagar : Aitor Mujica (GK), Jared Gallagher (Marcus Mosses 66’), Lazar Vujanic, Yuki Aizu, Boris Kopitovic (C) (Anaqi Ismit 82’), Riku Fukashiro, Naqiuddin Eunos (Samuel Pillai 82’), Alejandro Masogo, Marvin Anieboh, Kieran Teo (Syed Akmal 82’), Syahrul Sazali (Madhu Mohana 21’)
 Unused subs: Kenji Rusydi (GK), Travis Ang (GK), Fathullah Rahmat, Zahil Rahman, Darius Lai
 Stags keep perfect record intact 
 Jurong 2-3 Tampines | Jurong East | 25 October 
 Seiya Satsukida 47’, Tyler Ho 90+2’ | Yuki Kobayashi 23’, Hide Higashikawa 41’, Kohya Kazama 45+2’  
 Tampines Rovers survived a spirited second-half fightback from FC Jurong to secure a 3-2 victory and maintain their perfect start to the season. 
 The Stags enjoyed a memorable first half, racing into a three-goal lead before the break. Kobayashi opened the scoring in the 23rd minute with a stunning effort into the top corner, before Higashikawa doubled Tampines’ advantage in the 41st minute with a powerful strike that went in off the underside of the bar. Kazama then added a third just before half-time, heading home Kenshin Yamazaki’s cross from the right flank.
 Jurong responded just two minutes after the restart through Seiya Satsukida, whose effort slipped through Tampines goalkeeper Syazwan Buhari’s grasp.  Ho then reduced the deficit further in the second minute of stoppage time, turning Keisuke Honda’s corner home off his thigh. 
 However, it proved too little, too late for Jurong, who slumped to their third consecutive defeat of the season.
 Facts 
 Seiya Satsukida scored his first goal for FC Jurong.
 Jurong’s Tyler Ho scored his first professional goal on his SPL debut.
 Jurong’s Hazeem Bakre, formerly of Middlesbrough Under-21s, made his SPL debut as a substitute.
 Tampines goalkeeper Syazwan Buhari made his 300th SPL appearance.
 Tampines’ Jacob Mahler registered his first SPL assist since 14 August 2021, when he set up Khairin Nadim for Young Lions against Balestier. It was also his first assist for the Stags since 20 August 2025, when he set up the win over Philippines’ Cebu FC in the Shopee Cup. 
 The last goalless draw between Jurong and Tampines came on 24 September 2021, with both sides scoring in each of their last 19 meetings across all competitions.
 Jurong: Hassan Sunny (GK), Kim Yoonsik, Shunsuke Ono (Keisuke Honda 82’), Yuma Tsuzurabara, Seiya Satsukida (C), Mizuki Ando (Hazeem Bakre 66’), Toa Suenaga (Takuma Yamaguchi 66’), Syed Firdaus Hassan, Sim Jun Yen (Tyler Ho 46’), Andrew Aw (Aneeq Fairus 79’), Lee Jaeyong
 Unused subs: Lee Jinwoo (GK), Seo Seungwoo, Kodai Dahi, Helmi Shahrol, Delwinder Singh, Aqil Zafri, Izz Anaqi
 Tampines: Syazwan Buhari (GK) (C), Jacob Mahler, Shah Shahiran, Shodai Yokoyama (Raoul Suhaimi 78’), Dylan Fox, Kenshin Yamazaki (Takeshi Yoshimoto 62’), Hide Higashikawa, Seiga Sumi (Ong Yu En 90+3’), Yuki Kobayashi (Faris Ramli 62’), Irfan Fandi, Kohya Kazama (Naberu Yoshitaka Furusawa 78’)
 Unused subs: Zharfan Rohaizad (GK), Jarec Ng (GK), Amirul Adli, Yuma Kimura, Amirul Haikal, Irfan Najeeb, Rasul Ramli
 Geylang see off Hougang to return to SPL summit 
 Geylang 3-0 Hougang | Our Tampines Hub | 26 October 
 Yang Hyeonju 45+2’, 90+1’, Kaisei Ogawa 53’ 
 Geylang cruised to a comfortable win over Hougang, condemning the Cheetahs to a fourth consecutive defeat in the SPL.
 Yang capitalised on a mistake by Hougang captain Zulqarnaen Suzliman to break the deadlock in first-half stoppage time, before Ogawa doubled Geylang’s advantage in the 53rd minute, calmly finishing after being picked out by compatriot Ryoya Taniguchi’s reverse pass.
 Hougang’s hopes of mounting a comeback suffered a further blow in the 75th minute when Milos Drincic was sent off after receiving his second yellow card.
 Yang then completed his brace in stoppage time, chesting down Milos Cupic’s pass before finishing emphatically to seal a convincing win for the Eagles, who returned to the top of the SPL, with the Eastern Derby within the horizon.
 Facts 
 Yang Hyeonju bagged his second brace of the season, having first scored twice against Young Lions in Matchweek 2.
 M Anumanthan made his first SPL start since 25 May 2025, when he featured for the Sailors against Tampines.
 Milos Drincic received Hougang’s fourth red card of the season, following dismissals for Zulqarnaen Suzliman, Huzaifah Aziz and Khairin Nadim.
 Milos Cupic became the first goalkeeper since Sailors’ Ivan Susak on 8 February 2026 to register an assist in the SPL.
 With one draw and four defeats so far, Hougang have made their worst SPL start since 2023, when they recorded one win and four losses in their opening five matches.
 Geylang are off to their best start to any SPL season since their title-winning 2001 campaign, where they also picked up four wins and one draw in their opening five matches.
 Geylang: Milos Cupic (GK), Darren Teh, Cho Eunsu, Kim Taeuk, Naoki Yoshioka (Raiyan Noor 90+4’), M Anumanthan (Sahil Suhaimi 71’), Kaisei Ogawa (Nur Ikhsanuddin 90+4’), Joshua Pereira (C), Ryoya Taniguchi (Dejan Racic 71’), Harith Kanadi (Alessandro Mika Lura 87’), Yang Hyeonju 
 Unused subs: Aniq Matin (GK), Dylan Pereira (GK), S C Denilson, Prince Rio Rifae’i, Diego Aspiras, Milan Landreman, Daniel Serrano
 Hougang: Ridhuan Barudin (GK), Mahame Siby, Jordan Vestering, Huzaifah Aziz (Arya Igami 57’), Zulqarnaen Suzliman (C) (Natthakit Phosri 57’), Saifullah Akbar, Ayman Kassimi (Amir Syafiz 69’), Milos Drincic, Oakley Cannonier (Khairin Nadim 69’), Lucas Cardoso, Jordan Emaviwe
 Unused subs: Takahiro Koga (GK), Aizil Yazid (GK), Washington Jaramillo, Samuel Billington, Connor Flynn-Gillespie, Phutanet Somjit, Brant Tan, Jarrel Ong
